user_profile.other_preferences: Want to focus Global Market,Intermediate (Built small projects) coding experience, familiar with python, java, C, C++ Language and familiar with Tensorflow,Pytorch Framework. build some academic projects. passionate in harware software integration work

prompt_used:
I want to become a Computer Vision Engineer. I have 5 months to prepare and I can study 1 hours per day. 
My experience level is University Recent CSE Graduate. Want to focus Global Market,Intermediate (Built small projects) coding experience, familiar with python, java, C, C++ Language and familiar with Tensorflow,Pytorch Framework. build some academic projects. passionate in harware software integration work
Now generate a learning plan for me.

topics: Python for Data Science Refresher (Numpy, Pandas, Matplotlib for image manipulation)
OpenCV Basics: Image loading, saving, display, pixel access
Color Spaces (RGB, BGR, HSV, Grayscale)
daily_activities: Review Numpy/Pandas/Matplotlib docs/tutorials (30 min)
Basic OpenCV operations coding practice (load/save/display, color conversions) (30 min)

topics: Image Processing Fundamentals: Filters (Gaussian, Median, Bilateral blur, Sharpening)
Thresholding (Simple, Adaptive, Otsu's)
Morphological Operations (Erosion, Dilation, Opening, Closing)
daily_activities: Read about filter types and their applications (20 min)
Implement various filters and morphological operations with OpenCV (40 min)

topics: Geometric Transformations: Resizing, Rotation, Translation, Affine/Perspective Transforms
Image Histograms and Equalization
Contour Detection and Analysis (area, perimeter, bounding box)
daily_activities: Understand transform matrices and histogram concepts (25 min)
Practice applying transforms and contour detection (35 min)

topics: Edge Detection (Canny, Sobel, Prewitt)
Feature Detection: Harris Corner, ORB/BRISK (conceptual understanding & OpenCV usage)
Introduction to Object Tracking (e.g., MeanShift/CamShift - conceptual)
daily_activities: Explore different edge detectors and feature descriptors (20 min)
Apply Canny edge detection and explore ORB features with OpenCV (40 min)
Review concepts of traditional tracking algorithms

project_ideas: Create a simple image editor (filters, resize, rotate)
Build an object counter for a static image (e.g., counting shapes)

learning_plan.focus_area: Deep Learning for Computer Vision - Basics

topics: CNN Architectures Review: LeNet, AlexNet, VGG
Understanding Convolutional Layers, Pooling Layers, Activation Functions
Introduction to PyTorch/TensorFlow for image tasks (datasets, dataloaders)
daily_activities: Review CNN building blocks and popular early architectures (30 min)
Set up basic image classification pipeline in PyTorch/TensorFlow (30 min)

topics: Advanced CNNs: ResNet, Inception, MobileNet (conceptual understanding)
Transfer Learning Concepts: Why it's effective, fine-tuning vs. feature extraction
Using pre-trained models (e.g., torchvision.models or tf.keras.applications)
daily_activities: Understand modern CNN architectural innovations (25 min)
Implement a simple transfer learning example using a pre-trained model (e.g., ResNet-50) (35 min)

topics: Practical Image Classification: Training a model on a small custom dataset
Data Augmentation Techniques (random crop, flip, rotation, color jitter)
Loss Functions (Cross-Entropy) and Optimizers (SGD, Adam)
daily_activities: Apply data augmentation to a dataset (20 min)
Train a transfer learning model for image classification (40 min)

topics: Evaluation Metrics for Classification: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, Confusion Matrix
Hyperparameter Tuning Basics (learning rate, batch size)
Understanding Overfitting and Underfitting, Regularization techniques (Dropout, L2)
daily_activities: Calculate and interpret classification metrics (30 min)
Experiment with basic hyperparameter tuning or regularization (30 min)

key_skills: Building and training CNNs with PyTorch/TensorFlow
project_ideas: Image classifier for a custom dataset (e.g., different types of leaves, local animals)
Implement a simple GAN for image generation (conceptual understanding & using existing code)
resources: 'Deep Learning with Python' by François Chollet
'Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow' by Aurélien Géron
fast.ai Practical Deep Learning for Coders course (relevant sections)

learning_plan.focus_area: Deep Learning for Computer Vision - Advanced

topics: Object Detection I: R-CNN family (R-CNN, Fast R-CNN, Faster R-CNN) - conceptual understanding
Bounding Boxes, Intersection over Union (IoU) metric
Non-Max Suppression (NMS)
daily_activities: Read about region proposal networks and two-stage detectors (30 min)
Code IoU and NMS from scratch (or review implementations) (30 min)

topics: Object Detection II: YOLO & SSD - conceptual understanding, advantages for real-time
Anchor Boxes
Practical inference with pre-trained YOLO/SSD models (e.g., YOLOv5/v8, SSD MobileNet)
daily_activities: Understand single-shot detectors (YOLO, SSD) (25 min)
Run inference with a pre-trained YOLO model on images/videos (e.g., using Ultralytics YOLO) (35 min)

topics: Semantic Segmentation: FCN, U-Net - conceptual understanding
Introduction to pixel-wise classification
Practical inference with pre-trained segmentation models
daily_activities: Explore semantic segmentation architectures (25 min)
Use a pre-trained segmentation model (e.g., DeepLabV3, U-Net) for inference (35 min)

topics: Instance Segmentation: Mask R-CNN - conceptual understanding (combining object detection & segmentation)
Evaluation Metrics for Object Detection (mAP - Mean Average Precision)
Understanding common CV datasets (COCO, PASCAL VOC)
daily_activities: Understand the difference between semantic and instance segmentation (30 min)
Read about mAP calculation and dataset formats (30 min)

key_skills: Understanding of object detection algorithms (YOLO, SSD, R-CNN family)
Understanding of segmentation algorithms (U-Net, FCN, Mask R-CNN)
project_ideas: Implement real-time object detection using a pre-trained YOLO model on a webcam feed
Road segmentation using a pre-trained model
resources: Papers With Code for object detection/segmentation
Towards Data Science articles on advanced CV topics

topics: Transformer-based Vision Models: ViT (Vision Transformer) basics, Swin Transformer (conceptual)
Review of attention mechanisms in vision
Self-supervised learning basics (conceptual)
daily_activities: Understand the core idea of ViT and how transformers are applied to images (30 min)
Explore high-level concepts of self-supervised learning for CV (30 min)

topics: Introduction to Object Tracking: Simple online tracking methods (e.g., SORT, DeepSORT - conceptual)
Multiple Object Tracking (MOT) challenges and approaches
Basics of Video Processing with OpenCV and Deep Learning
daily_activities: Read about different object tracking algorithms (25 min)
Experiment with applying pre-trained object detection to video frames (35 min)

topics: Edge AI & Model Deployment Fundamentals: Quantization, Pruning, Knowledge Distillation
Model Conversion Formats (ONNX, TFLite)
Introduction to deployment tools (TensorRT, OpenVINO - conceptual understanding)
daily_activities: Understand model optimization techniques for edge devices (30 min)
Convert a simple PyTorch/TensorFlow model to ONNX/TFLite (30 min)

topics: Hardware-Software Integration Concepts: Understanding constraints of embedded devices (memory, computation, power)
Exploring platforms like NVIDIA Jetson, Raspberry Pi (with NCS/Coral) - conceptual
Building a basic API for a CV model using Flask/Streamlit for model serving
daily_activities: Research different edge computing platforms and their use cases (30 min)
Develop a simple Flask/Streamlit application to serve a pre-trained image classifier (30 min)

key_skills: Conceptual understanding of advanced CV models (Transformers)
Understanding of edge AI hardware and software integration concepts
project_ideas: Explore a pre-trained ViT for image classification
Build a web API to serve an object detection model
Research and plan a project for a specific edge device (e.g., Jetson Nano)
resources: Articles on model optimization for deployment

topics: Capstone Project Planning: Define problem, data requirements, model selection, deployment strategy
Refine problem statement and project scope based on learned skills
Dataset exploration and preparation for the chosen project
daily_activities: Brainstorm and select a capstone project idea (e.g., real-time object counter, custom object detection for a specific task, gesture recognition, traffic monitoring) (60 min)
Start collecting/preparing data for the project (60 min)

topics: Capstone Project Implementation: Model selection and initial training
Code structure and modularity
Iterative development and debugging
daily_activities: Implement initial model code (e.g., fine-tuning a pre-trained detector) (60 min)
Address early bugs and refine code (60 min)

topics: Capstone Project Evaluation and Optimization
Rigorous testing and evaluation of model performance
Experiment with optimization techniques (e.g., hyperparameter tuning, model pruning/quantization if relevant)
daily_activities: Evaluate model performance using appropriate metrics (60 min)
Iterate on model training/optimization (60 min)

topics: Capstone Project Deployment (simulated or actual)
Documenting the project (GitHub README, project report)
Portfolio building & Resume enhancement
Networking and job search strategies
daily_activities: Finalize project deployment strategy and implement (e.g., create a Docker container, deploy to a local API, prepare for edge device if chosen) (60 min)
Prepare a comprehensive GitHub repository, update resume, practice explaining project (60 min)

project_ideas: Your chosen capstone project, leveraging multiple skills learned across the months.
resources: Online communities (Reddit r/computervision, CVPR/ECCV/ICCV papers for inspiration)

general_advice: Consistency is key: 1 hour every day is more effective than cramming once a week.
Prioritize understanding concepts over implementing everything from scratch. Leverage libraries and pre-trained models.
Actively participate in online communities or forums for questions and discussions.
Follow leading researchers and companies in CV on social media (e.g., X/Twitter, LinkedIn) to stay updated.
Focus on practical applications and build a strong portfolio on GitHub with well-documented projects.
For 'hardware-software integration,' consider purchasing a low-cost device like a Raspberry Pi 4 or Jetson Nano in month 4 if budget and time allow for deeper hands-on experience.
